messages:
maria: Quick heads-up: saw a perf regression on latest runtime branch when running multi-gpu TP+PP loads with large KV caches. All-reduce time jumped ~2x on the decode path.

sam: uh — which config? TP=2 PP=2? model/seq len?

maria: TP=2 PP=2 DP=1, seq=2048, batch=8. Profiling trace attached (perf-bot posted). KV shards distributed by tensor-parallel split; during decode we see frequent small all-reduces for KV sync.

perf-bot: perf trace: http://perf/reports/1742001234 (summary: all-reduce total 220ms -> 470ms after merge)

lee: Small all-reduces are killer. We should either: 1) switch KV sharding to DP (replicate per device) to remove comm during decode, or 2) batch the KV all-reduces and overlap with compute. Memory cost vs latency tradeoff.

anya: Memory headroom on infra nodes is tight. DP replication will blow memory for 70B-ish models. Can we do async NCCL allreduce on a separate stream and ensure compute on main stream runs while comm is inflight?

devon: We tried async allreduce last quarter but kernel selector kept spawning tiny kernels on same stream, so overlap didn't happen. Kernel selector chooses per-op kernel based on sequence length distribution; looks like for short tails it picked non-fused kernels with lower launch latency but worse occupancy.

maria: Right — kernel selection regression: new selector prioritizes minimal latency per op, ends up increasing kernel count -> reduces ability to overlap. Profiling shows GPU occupancy drops during decode step.

sam: Immediate mitigation: add a runtime flag to prefer fused-kernel families (force_fused_kernels=true) and increase batching window to 20ms so small requests coalesce. That reduces all-reduce count and increases op size.

lee: For KV sharding strategy: suggest hybrid: shard KV across PP/TP for weight matrices but replicate for attention past KV (DP-like cache replication for last-kv) — basically keep last-KV local per GPU for serving to avoid cross-GPU reads during decode, and periodically sync checkpoints for beam search.

anya: Hybrid sounds promising. Also consider chunked KV transfer: on first token, warm local cache by fetching hot prefixes only, lazy fetch rest. That reduces immediate all-reduce bandwidth.

devon: I'll open a small PR with: 1) toggle for fused kernel preference 2) batching-window increase 3) KV-shard mode enum {dp, tp, hybrid_lazy}. We need perf tests across TP/PP/DP combos.

maria: :thumbsup: Can we add a trace tag in console showing per-step comm vs compute breakdown? That would make regressions obvious.

perf-bot: Scheduled nightly benchmark: multi-gpu-TPPP-KV-1742001234 -> run queued.

sam: Assigning follow-ups: @devon (PR), @lee (design doc for hybrid shard), @anya (async allreduce repro). Let's sync tomorrow 10am. I'll capture perf traces.

maria: Thanks all — logging action items in #eng-runtime-weekly.

```bash
# quick repro command (devon will add to PR)
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_PREFER_FUSED=1
export REDWOOD_KV_SHARD_MODE=hybrid_lazy
python -m redwood.runtime.bench --model tgi-70b --tp 2 --pp 2 --batch 8 --seq 2048
```
